This is a deliberate separation: authentication, upload, virus scanning, task management and final storage do not depend on the same service.

Why these choices?

  • background_downloader uses native Android WorkManager and Apple's background URLSession mechanisms. It supports persistent transfer tracking and retry behaviour.

    Dart API docs+2

  • Firebase provides user authentication and a database for approval and task records.

    Firebase+1

  • Cloudflare R2 gives us a temporary storage area with a 10 GB monthly free storage allowance and free internet egress.

    Cloudflare R2 docs+1

2. Exact upload workflow

1. Scanner creates PDF

PDF is saved permanently in the app's local documents directory before any network operation.

2. Upload gateway receives PDF

Checks the user's approval, file size, file signature and upload ID.

3. Quarantine and validation

Stores a temporary copy in R2, scans it with ClamAV, parses the PDF and checks for dangerous embedded content.

4. OneDrive delivery

Cloud Run uses your authorised Microsoft connection to upload the clean PDF.

5. Delivery verification

Checks the returned OneDrive file ID, file size and destination before marking the upload complete.

Delivered to ATTAIR OneDrive

Temporary copy is retained for seven days, then deleted automatically.

If OneDrive is unavailable, the verified PDF remains in R2 with status Awaiting OneDrive delivery. The server retries. It does not ask the user to scan again.

3. OneDrive connection: the first and most important test

Your account is:

isaac.eke@attair.com.ng

I would use a single server-side Microsoft Graph delegated connection, authorised by you once.

The application registration must belong to your own project. We will not reuse the Microsoft-owned client ID that caused AADSTS65002.

The intended permissions are:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Files.ReadWrite allows the application to write files to the signed-in user's OneDrive without inherently requiring administrator consent. However, ATTAIR's tenant policy can still require administrator approval.

Microsoft Learn+1

Important security limitation: This delegated permission is broader than one folder. The backend will be programmed to write only to ATTAIR Techlog Uploads, but the underlying Microsoft token has access to your OneDrive files more broadly. Its credentials must never be exposed to the mobile app.

The go/no-go test

Before implementing the rest of the system:

  1. Register your own application in Microsoft Entra.

  2. Configure its server-side redirect URI.

  3. Sign in using your ATTAIR account.

  4. Authorise the delegated permissions.

  5. Upload one test PDF through Microsoft Graph.

  6. Verify that it appears in the actual OneDrive folder.

If you cannot register an app or ATTAIR blocks user consent, stop here and request the necessary approval from IT. There is no reliable way to bypass that organisational restriction.

I would not spend another development cycle on the scanner until this test passes.

4. File validation and antivirus

Every uploaded file must pass these checks.

Check

Required behaviour

Extension

Must be .pdf

MIME type

Must indicate PDF

File signature

Must contain a valid PDF header

PDF parser

Must successfully parse the document

Structural check

qpdf must report no structural errors

Malware scan

ClamAV must report clean

Active content

Reject dangerous JavaScript, launch actions and embedded executable content

File size

Maximum 10 MB

Duplicate detection

SHA-256 hash and unique upload ID

A file that fails validation goes into quarantine. It never reaches OneDrive.

One qualification: antivirus scanning cannot prove that a file is harmless. It detects known threats and suspicious structures; it cannot guarantee detection of every malicious PDF.

I would preserve the original PDF rather than automatically rewriting or flattening it during security checks. Aircraft records should not be silently altered.

5. Comments and tasks

This needs to be built into the data model from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

I would support three ways of creating tasks.

A. Comments typed in the scanner

Example:

Check the aircraft hours against the previous techlog.

The app sends the comment with the PDF. The server creates a task linked to that document.

B. Comments written directly on the PDF

The scanner should have an annotation tool supporting:

  • Sticky-note comments

  • Text annotations

  • Highlighted text with a comment

  • Page-specific comments

The annotation content and page number are saved as task records. Supported annotations are also embedded into the PDF.

C. Comments added later

Users can reopen an existing document record and add comments. These create new tasks linked to the original PDF.

If someone edits a PDF in an external PDF editor, they must re-import the revised PDF for its supported annotations to be extracted. We should not promise automatic detection of changes made in arbitrary external applications.

Example task screen

Techlog tasks

AIRCRAFT 001 · TECHLOG 1501

Open

Check aircraft hours against previous techlog

Page 2 · Comment from Pilot A

TECHLOG 1502

In progress

Verify landing time entry

Page 1 · PDF annotation

TECHLOG 1503

Completed

Confirm missing signature

Page 3 · Comment from Pilot B

Each task should have an owner, creation date, source PDF, page number, status, and optional resolution comment.

This is the implementation brief I would use. It deliberately prohibits rebuilding the scanner or skipping the proof-of-connection stage.

Writing

ATTAIR Techlog Scanner — Cloud Upload and Task System

Objective

Implement a reliable, cloud-based PDF submission system for the existing Flutter aircraft techlog scanner.

The existing scanner is working. Preserve it.

Do not rebuild, redesign or replace its camera, cropping, page navigation, PDF generation or existing scanning workflow.

Approved technology stack

  • Flutter: existing application

  • Background transfers: background_downloader 9.6.5, subject to project compatibility testing

  • Authentication: Firebase Authentication, email/password and email verification

  • Database: Cloud Firestore

  • Backend: Python FastAPI on Google Cloud Run

  • Temporary file storage: private Cloudflare R2 bucket

  • Antivirus: ClamAV with updated signatures

  • PDF validation and annotation extraction: PyMuPDF and qpdf

  • Final storage: Isaac's existing ATTAIR OneDrive account

  • OneDrive API: Microsoft Graph using an application registered specifically for this project

Mandatory implementation rules

  1. Work from a backup or Git checkpoint.

  2. Inspect the existing project before changing anything.

  3. Document current scanner functionality and existing dependencies.

  4. Do not change unrelated scanner code.

  5. Do not place Microsoft credentials, R2 credentials or backend secrets in Flutter.

  6. Do not use a Microsoft-owned first-party application ID.

  7. Never mark a file uploaded merely because an HTTP request succeeded.

  8. Preserve the original PDF.

  9. Never delete a local PDF before verified final delivery.

  10. Implement and test each phase independently.

Phase 0 — OneDrive proof of connection

Before implementing the upload system, register an application with its own client ID.

Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Implement the server-side authorisation flow.

Authenticate Isaac's ATTAIR account, upload a test PDF into the designated OneDrive folder and verify the resulting file ID and size.

If application registration or consent is blocked by ATTAIR's tenant, stop. Report the exact error. Do not attempt alternative first-party client IDs or unapproved authentication workarounds.

Phase 1 — Accounts and approvals

Implement Firebase email/password authentication and email verification.

New accounts have pending status.

An administrator can approve, reject or revoke users.

Only server-controlled approval records determine upload eligibility.

The scanner remains usable while approval is pending.

Phase 2 — Upload gateway

Implement a FastAPI service on Cloud Run.

Every upload must:

  • Require a valid Firebase ID token.

  • Check current approval status.

  • Have a unique upload ID.

  • Enforce a 10 MB maximum.

  • Verify the PDF signature and MIME type.

  • Calculate SHA-256.

  • Reject duplicate submissions safely.

  • Store a temporary copy in private R2 storage.

Phase 3 — Security validation

Use ClamAV with current virus signatures.

Use PyMuPDF and qpdf to inspect the PDF.

Reject corrupt PDFs and dangerous embedded active content.

Quarantine suspicious files.

Do not upload quarantined files to OneDrive.

Record the scan result and validation details.

Phase 4 — OneDrive delivery

Use the server-side Microsoft Graph connection.

Write only to the configured ATTAIR TECHLOG UPLOADS folder.

Retain verified temporary files when OneDrive is unavailable.

Retry failed deliveries without creating duplicates.

Verify the resulting OneDrive file ID, size and destination before setting the status to delivered.

Keep temporary copies for seven days after confirmed delivery, then delete them.

Phase 5 — Comments and tasks

Implement:

  • Typed comments associated with a PDF.

  • In-app PDF sticky notes and text annotations.

  • Highlight comments.

  • Extraction of supported annotations from submitted PDFs.

  • Comments added later to existing document records.

  • Task creation, assignment and status updates.

Every task must reference its source PDF and page number where applicable.

Phase 6 — Mobile integration

Integrate the upload queue into the existing scanner.

Save the PDF locally before starting upload.

Use native background transfer support.

Persist upload state across application restarts.

Retry interrupted transfers and reconcile server status.

Do not delete local documents until verified OneDrive delivery and explicit local retention rules permit it.

Phase 7 — Acceptance testing

Test Android and iOS separately.

Test valid PDFs, corrupt PDFs, EICAR antivirus test files, duplicate uploads, interrupted connections, expired tokens, revoked users, OneDrive outages and comment extraction.

Regression-test all existing scanner functionality.

Do not declare completion until the acceptance tests pass.

Reporting requirements

After each phase, report:

  • Files created or changed.

  • Exact dependencies and versions.

  • Tests executed.

  • Test results.

  • Known limitations.

  • Whether the phase is safe to proceed.

Do not silently skip failed tests or claim success without evidence.

2. How we connect to your OneDrive

There is a potentially simpler route than the application-permission architecture I initially described.

Use Microsoft Graph delegated authentication, with you signing into your ATTAIR account once during administrator setup.

The flow would be:

  1. Register your own application in Microsoft Entra.

  2. Request the delegated Files.ReadWrite permission.

  3. You sign in with your ATTAIR account and authorise the connection.

  4. The backend securely stores the authentication credentials needed to maintain that connection.

  5. Approved users upload PDFs to the backend.

  6. The backend uploads those PDFs into your OneDrive folder.

Microsoft documents Files.ReadWrite as allowing an application to create, update and delete files belonging to the signed-in user. Its permission reference indicates that this delegated permission does not inherently require administrator consent. However, ATTAIR's tenant policies can still block user consent.

Microsoft Learn+1

Important security detail: The OneDrive credentials must stay on the backend, never inside the Android application. Also, this permission grants access to your files more broadly than just one folder, so the backend must strictly restrict its own operations to the designated upload folder.

If ATTAIR blocks delegated consent, we will need its IT administrator to approve the connection. We cannot bypass that policy.

5. Reliability rules I would make mandatory

My final recommendation: a small upload gateway + OneDrive

I would not use Telegram, email or Dropbox as the primary architecture.

I would build a small private upload website/API, with a lightweight backend, and connect that backend to your ATTAIR OneDrive through a Windows OneDrive Sync Bridge.

This avoids Microsoft OAuth inside the mobile app entirely. It also avoids giving every user access to your storage account.

The workflow is:

  1. User scans a techlog.

  2. App creates a PDF.

  3. App submits the PDF automatically to your upload server.

  4. Server verifies the file and checks it for malicious content.

  5. Server places the verified PDF in a local folder synchronised by your ATTAIR OneDrive desktop client.

  6. OneDrive synchronises it to your cloud account.

  7. Your app receives confirmation after the file is verified in the OneDrive destination.

This is a separate feature I would build into the same upload system.

For example, a user submits a scanned PDF and adds:

Check the aircraft hours against the previous techlog.

The app sends the PDF and comment together.

The server records:

  • PDF identifier

  • Aircraft registration

  • Techlog number

  • Comment

  • User who submitted it

  • Submission date

  • Task status

Your app then displays:

I would also support comments added after the PDF has been uploaded. They should attach to the existing PDF rather than creating another copy.

5. The reliability requirements

These are non-negotiable:

  1. Local PDF saved before upload.

  2. Upload queue survives app closure and phone restart.

  3. Automatic retry after internet interruption.

  4. Server acknowledges receipt only after validation.

  5. OneDrive status remains separate from server-received status.

  6. Unique upload IDs prevent duplicates.

  7. No local PDF deletion until OneDrive synchronisation is confirmed.

  8. Failed uploads are visible and can be retried manually.

The app should show three distinct statuses:

  • Saved on phone

  • Received and verified

  • Stored in ATTAIR OneDrive

That prevents the app from claiming success prematurely.

2. Exact upload workflow

1. Scanner creates PDF

PDF is saved permanently in the app's local documents directory before any network operation.

2. Upload gateway receives PDF

Checks the user's approval, file size, file signature and upload ID.

3. Quarantine and validation

Stores a temporary copy in R2, scans it with ClamAV, parses the PDF and checks for dangerous embedded content.

4. OneDrive delivery

Cloud Run uses your authorised Microsoft connection to upload the clean PDF.

5. Delivery verification

Checks the returned OneDrive file ID, file size and destination before marking the upload complete.

Delivered to ATTAIR OneDrive

Temporary copy is retained for seven days, then deleted automatically.

If OneDrive is unavailable, the verified PDF remains in R2 with status Awaiting OneDrive delivery. The server retries. It does not ask the user to scan again.

3. OneDrive connection: the first and most important test

Your account is:

isaac.eke@attair.com.ng

I would use a single server-side Microsoft Graph delegated connection, authorised by you once.

The application registration must belong to your own project. We will not reuse the Microsoft-owned client ID that caused AADSTS65002.

The intended permissions are:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Files.ReadWrite allows the application to write files to the signed-in user's OneDrive without inherently requiring administrator consent. However, ATTAIR's tenant policy can still require administrator approval.

Microsoft Learn+1

Important security limitation: This delegated permission is broader than one folder. The backend will be programmed to write only to ATTAIR Techlog Uploads, but the underlying Microsoft token has access to your OneDrive files more broadly. Its credentials must never be exposed to the mobile app.

The go/no-go test

Before implementing the rest of the system:

  1. Register your own application in Microsoft Entra.

  2. Configure its server-side redirect URI.

  3. Sign in using your ATTAIR account.

  4. Authorise the delegated permissions.

  5. Upload one test PDF through Microsoft Graph.

  6. Verify that it appears in the actual OneDrive folder.

If you cannot register an app or ATTAIR blocks user consent, stop here and request the necessary approval from IT. There is no reliable way to bypass that organisational restriction.

I would not spend another development cycle on the scanner until this test passes.

One qualification: antivirus scanning cannot prove that a file is harmless. It detects known threats and suspicious structures; it cannot guarantee detection of every malicious PDF.

5. Comments and tasks

This needs to be built into the data model from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

I would support three ways of creating tasks.

A. Comments typed in the scanner

Example:

Check the aircraft hours against the previous techlog.

The app sends the comment with the PDF. The server creates a task linked to that document.

B. Comments written directly on the PDF

The scanner should have an annotation tool supporting:

  • Sticky-note comments

  • Text annotations

  • Highlighted text with a comment

  • Page-specific comments

The annotation content and page number are saved as task records. Supported annotations are also embedded into the PDF.

C. Comments added later

Users can reopen an existing document record and add comments. These create new tasks linked to the original PDF.

If someone edits a PDF in an external PDF editor, they must re-import the revised PDF for its supported annotations to be extracted. We should not promise automatic detection of changes made in arbitrary external applications.

This is the implementation brief I would use. It deliberately prohibits rebuilding the scanner or skipping the proof-of-connection stage.

Writing

ATTAIR Techlog Scanner — Cloud Upload and Task System

Objective

Implement a reliable, cloud-based PDF submission system for the existing Flutter aircraft techlog scanner.

The existing scanner is working. Preserve it.

Do not rebuild, redesign or replace its camera, cropping, page navigation, PDF generation or existing scanning workflow.

Approved technology stack

  • Flutter: existing application

  • Background transfers: background_downloader 9.6.5, subject to project compatibility testing

  • Authentication: Firebase Authentication, email/password and email verification

  • Database: Cloud Firestore

  • Backend: Python FastAPI on Google Cloud Run

  • Temporary file storage: private Cloudflare R2 bucket

  • Antivirus: ClamAV with updated signatures

  • PDF validation and annotation extraction: PyMuPDF and qpdf

  • Final storage: Isaac's existing ATTAIR OneDrive account

  • OneDrive API: Microsoft Graph using an application registered specifically for this project

Mandatory implementation rules

  1. Work from a backup or Git checkpoint.

  2. Inspect the existing project before changing anything.

  3. Document current scanner functionality and existing dependencies.

  4. Do not change unrelated scanner code.

  5. Do not place Microsoft credentials, R2 credentials or backend secrets in Flutter.

  6. Do not use a Microsoft-owned first-party application ID.

  7. Never mark a file uploaded merely because an HTTP request succeeded.

  8. Preserve the original PDF.

  9. Never delete a local PDF before verified final delivery.

  10. Implement and test each phase independently.

Phase 0 — OneDrive proof of connection

Before implementing the upload system, register an application with its own client ID.

Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Implement the server-side authorisation flow.

Authenticate Isaac's ATTAIR account, upload a test PDF into the designated OneDrive folder and verify the resulting file ID and size.

If application registration or consent is blocked by ATTAIR's tenant, stop. Report the exact error. Do not attempt alternative first-party client IDs or unapproved authentication workarounds.

Phase 1 — Accounts and approvals

Implement Firebase email/password authentication and email verification.

New accounts have pending status.

An administrator can approve, reject or revoke users.

Only server-controlled approval records determine upload eligibility.

The scanner remains usable while approval is pending.

Phase 2 — Upload gateway

Implement a FastAPI service on Cloud Run.

Every upload must:

  • Require a valid Firebase ID token.

  • Check current approval status.

  • Have a unique upload ID.

  • Enforce a 10 MB maximum.

  • Verify the PDF signature and MIME type.

  • Calculate SHA-256.

  • Reject duplicate submissions safely.

  • Store a temporary copy in private R2 storage.

Phase 3 — Security validation

Use ClamAV with current virus signatures.

Use PyMuPDF and qpdf to inspect the PDF.

Reject corrupt PDFs and dangerous embedded active content.

Quarantine suspicious files.

Do not upload quarantined files to OneDrive.

Record the scan result and validation details.

Phase 4 — OneDrive delivery

Use the server-side Microsoft Graph connection.

Write only to the configured ATTAIR TECHLOG UPLOADS folder.

Retain verified temporary files when OneDrive is unavailable.

Retry failed deliveries without creating duplicates.

Verify the resulting OneDrive file ID, size and destination before setting the status to delivered.

Keep temporary copies for seven days after confirmed delivery, then delete them.

Phase 5 — Comments and tasks

Implement:

  • Typed comments associated with a PDF.

  • In-app PDF sticky notes and text annotations.

  • Highlight comments.

  • Extraction of supported annotations from submitted PDFs.

  • Comments added later to existing document records.

  • Task creation, assignment and status updates.

Every task must reference its source PDF and page number where applicable.

Phase 6 — Mobile integration

Integrate the upload queue into the existing scanner.

Save the PDF locally before starting upload.

Use native background transfer support.

Persist upload state across application restarts.

Retry interrupted transfers and reconcile server status.

Do not delete local documents until verified OneDrive delivery and explicit local retention rules permit it.

Phase 7 — Acceptance testing

Test Android and iOS separately.

Test valid PDFs, corrupt PDFs, EICAR antivirus test files, duplicate uploads, interrupted connections, expired tokens, revoked users, OneDrive outages and comment extraction.

Regression-test all existing scanner functionality.

Do not declare completion until the acceptance tests pass.

Reporting requirements

After each phase, report:

  • Files created or changed.

  • Exact dependencies and versions.

  • Tests executed.

  • Test results.

  • Known limitations.

  • Whether the phase is safe to proceed.

Do not silently skip failed tests or claim success without evidence.

5. The reliability requirements

These are non-negotiable:

  1. Local PDF saved before upload.

  2. Upload queue survives app closure and phone restart.

  3. Automatic retry after internet interruption.

  4. Server acknowledges receipt only after validation.

  5. OneDrive status remains separate from server-received status.

  6. Unique upload IDs prevent duplicates.

  7. No local PDF deletion until OneDrive synchronisation is confirmed.

  8. Failed uploads are visible and can be retried manually.

The app should show three distinct statuses:

  • Saved on phone

  • Received and verified

  • Stored in ATTAIR OneDrive

That prevents the app from claiming success prematurely.

3. OneDrive connection: the first and most important test

Your account is:

isaac.eke@attair.com.ng

I would use a single server-side Microsoft Graph delegated connection, authorised by you once.

The application registration must belong to your own project. We will not reuse the Microsoft-owned client ID that caused AADSTS65002.

The intended permissions are:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Files.ReadWrite allows the application to write files to the signed-in user's OneDrive without inherently requiring administrator consent. However, ATTAIR's tenant policy can still require administrator approval.

Microsoft Learn+1

Important security limitation: This delegated permission is broader than one folder. The backend will be programmed to write only to ATTAIR Techlog Uploads, but the underlying Microsoft token has access to your OneDrive files more broadly. Its credentials must never be exposed to the mobile app.

The go/no-go test

Before implementing the rest of the system:

  1. Register your own application in Microsoft Entra.

  2. Configure its server-side redirect URI.

  3. Sign in using your ATTAIR account.

  4. Authorise the delegated permissions.

  5. Upload one test PDF through Microsoft Graph.

  6. Verify that it appears in the actual OneDrive folder.

If you cannot register an app or ATTAIR blocks user consent, stop here and request the necessary approval from IT. There is no reliable way to bypass that organisational restriction.

I would not spend another development cycle on the scanner until this test passes.

5. Comments and tasks

This needs to be built into the data model from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

I would support three ways of creating tasks.

A. Comments typed in the scanner

Example:

Check the aircraft hours against the previous techlog.

The app sends the comment with the PDF. The server creates a task linked to that document.

B. Comments written directly on the PDF

The scanner should have an annotation tool supporting:

  • Sticky-note comments

  • Text annotations

  • Highlighted text with a comment

  • Page-specific comments

The annotation content and page number are saved as task records. Supported annotations are also embedded into the PDF.

C. Comments added later

Users can reopen an existing document record and add comments. These create new tasks linked to the original PDF.

If someone edits a PDF in an external PDF editor, they must re-import the revised PDF for its supported annotations to be extracted. We should not promise automatic detection of changes made in arbitrary external applications.

10. The instruction I would give the coding agent

This is the implementation brief I would use. It deliberately prohibits rebuilding the scanner or skipping the proof-of-connection stage.

Writing

ATTAIR Techlog Scanner — Cloud Upload and Task System

Objective

Implement a reliable, cloud-based PDF submission system for the existing Flutter aircraft techlog scanner.

The existing scanner is working. Preserve it.

Do not rebuild, redesign or replace its camera, cropping, page navigation, PDF generation or existing scanning workflow.

Approved technology stack

  • Flutter: existing application

  • Background transfers: background_downloader 9.6.5, subject to project compatibility testing

  • Authentication: Firebase Authentication, email/password and email verification

  • Database: Cloud Firestore

  • Backend: Python FastAPI on Google Cloud Run

  • Temporary file storage: private Cloudflare R2 bucket

  • Antivirus: ClamAV with updated signatures

  • PDF validation and annotation extraction: PyMuPDF and qpdf

  • Final storage: Isaac's existing ATTAIR OneDrive account

  • OneDrive API: Microsoft Graph using an application registered specifically for this project

Mandatory implementation rules

  1. Work from a backup or Git checkpoint.

  2. Inspect the existing project before changing anything.

  3. Document current scanner functionality and existing dependencies.

  4. Do not change unrelated scanner code.

  5. Do not place Microsoft credentials, R2 credentials or backend secrets in Flutter.

  6. Do not use a Microsoft-owned first-party application ID.

  7. Never mark a file uploaded merely because an HTTP request succeeded.

  8. Preserve the original PDF.

  9. Never delete a local PDF before verified final delivery.

  10. Implement and test each phase independently.

Phase 0 — OneDrive proof of connection

Before implementing the upload system, register an application with its own client ID.

Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Implement the server-side authorisation flow.

Authenticate Isaac's ATTAIR account, upload a test PDF into the designated OneDrive folder and verify the resulting file ID and size.

If application registration or consent is blocked by ATTAIR's tenant, stop. Report the exact error. Do not attempt alternative first-party client IDs or unapproved authentication workarounds.

Phase 1 — Accounts and approvals

Implement Firebase email/password authentication and email verification.

New accounts have pending status.

An administrator can approve, reject or revoke users.

Only server-controlled approval records determine upload eligibility.

The scanner remains usable while approval is pending.

Phase 2 — Upload gateway

Implement a FastAPI service on Cloud Run.

Every upload must:

  • Require a valid Firebase ID token.

  • Check current approval status.

  • Have a unique upload ID.

  • Enforce a 10 MB maximum.

  • Verify the PDF signature and MIME type.

  • Calculate SHA-256.

  • Reject duplicate submissions safely.

  • Store a temporary copy in private R2 storage.

Phase 3 — Security validation

Use ClamAV with current virus signatures.

Use PyMuPDF and qpdf to inspect the PDF.

Reject corrupt PDFs and dangerous embedded active content.

Quarantine suspicious files.

Do not upload quarantined files to OneDrive.

Record the scan result and validation details.

Phase 4 — OneDrive delivery

Use the server-side Microsoft Graph connection.

Write only to the configured ATTAIR TECHLOG UPLOADS folder.

Retain verified temporary files when OneDrive is unavailable.

Retry failed deliveries without creating duplicates.

Verify the resulting OneDrive file ID, size and destination before setting the status to delivered.

Keep temporary copies for seven days after confirmed delivery, then delete them.

Phase 5 — Comments and tasks

Implement:

  • Typed comments associated with a PDF.

  • In-app PDF sticky notes and text annotations.

  • Highlight comments.

  • Extraction of supported annotations from submitted PDFs.

  • Comments added later to existing document records.

  • Task creation, assignment and status updates.

Every task must reference its source PDF and page number where applicable.

Phase 6 — Mobile integration

Integrate the upload queue into the existing scanner.

Save the PDF locally before starting upload.

Use native background transfer support.

Persist upload state across application restarts.

Retry interrupted transfers and reconcile server status.

Do not delete local documents until verified OneDrive delivery and explicit local retention rules permit it.

Phase 7 — Acceptance testing

Test Android and iOS separately.

Test valid PDFs, corrupt PDFs, EICAR antivirus test files, duplicate uploads, interrupted connections, expired tokens, revoked users, OneDrive outages and comment extraction.

Regression-test all existing scanner functionality.

Do not declare completion until the acceptance tests pass.

Reporting requirements

After each phase, report:

  • Files created or changed.

  • Exact dependencies and versions.

  • Tests executed.

  • Test results.

  • Known limitations.

  • Whether the phase is safe to proceed.

Do not silently skip failed tests or claim success without evidence.

The first milestone should be very small: register one test account, approve it, upload one PDF, and verify that the PDF appears in your actual ATTAIR OneDrive folder. Only after that succeeds should the working scanner be connected to it.

I just want a small storage space. Think of "what is the most convenient/easiest means to send a pdf automatically on Android/iPhone reliably across all phone models?" It can be telegram, my custom website, mail app, Dropbox or whatever. I just want something with at least 100mb free storage and free unlimited uploads that will just confirm that the pdfs are actually genuine pdf files not viruses and my OneDrive has to be able to access that folder and move the PDFs. I also want some sort of way for comments on the scanned pdfs to appear as tasks in my app. I want the most widely researched methods guaranteed to work, one time. Cos one more try is just about the amount of patience I have left

My final recommendation: a small upload gateway + OneDrive

I would not use Telegram, email or Dropbox as the primary architecture.

I would build a small private upload website/API, with a lightweight backend, and connect that backend to your ATTAIR OneDrive through a Windows OneDrive Sync Bridge.

This avoids Microsoft OAuth inside the mobile app entirely. It also avoids giving every user access to your storage account.

The workflow is:

  1. User scans a techlog.

  2. App creates a PDF.

  3. App submits the PDF automatically to your upload server.

  4. Server verifies the file and checks it for malicious content.

  5. Server places the verified PDF in a local folder synchronised by your ATTAIR OneDrive desktop client.

  6. OneDrive synchronises it to your cloud account.

  7. Your app receives confirmation after the file is verified in the OneDrive destination.

5. The reliability requirements

These are non-negotiable:

  1. Local PDF saved before upload.

  2. Upload queue survives app closure and phone restart.

  3. Automatic retry after internet interruption.

  4. Server acknowledges receipt only after validation.

  5. OneDrive status remains separate from server-received status.

  6. Unique upload IDs prevent duplicates.

  7. No local PDF deletion until OneDrive synchronisation is confirmed.

  8. Failed uploads are visible and can be retried manually.

The app should show three distinct statuses:

  • Saved on phone

  • Received and verified

  • Stored in ATTAIR OneDrive

That prevents the app from claiming success prematurely.

2. Exact upload workflow

1. Scanner creates PDF

PDF is saved permanently in the app's local documents directory before any network operation.

2. Upload gateway receives PDF

Checks the user's approval, file size, file signature and upload ID.

3. Quarantine and validation

Stores a temporary copy in R2, scans it with ClamAV, parses the PDF and checks for dangerous embedded content.

4. OneDrive delivery

Cloud Run uses your authorised Microsoft connection to upload the clean PDF.

5. Delivery verification

Checks the returned OneDrive file ID, file size and destination before marking the upload complete.

Delivered to ATTAIR OneDrive

Temporary copy is retained for seven days, then deleted automatically.

If OneDrive is unavailable, the verified PDF remains in R2 with status Awaiting OneDrive delivery. The server retries. It does not ask the user to scan again.

3. OneDrive connection: the first and most important test

Your account is:

isaac.eke@attair.com.ng

I would use a single server-side Microsoft Graph delegated connection, authorised by you once.

The application registration must belong to your own project. We will not reuse the Microsoft-owned client ID that caused AADSTS65002.

The intended permissions are:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Files.ReadWrite allows the application to write files to the signed-in user's OneDrive without inherently requiring administrator consent. However, ATTAIR's tenant policy can still require administrator approval.

Microsoft Learn+1

Important security limitation: This delegated permission is broader than one folder. The backend will be programmed to write only to ATTAIR Techlog Uploads, but the underlying Microsoft token has access to your OneDrive files more broadly. Its credentials must never be exposed to the mobile app.

The go/no-go test

Before implementing the rest of the system:

  1. Register your own application in Microsoft Entra.

  2. Configure its server-side redirect URI.

  3. Sign in using your ATTAIR account.

  4. Authorise the delegated permissions.

  5. Upload one test PDF through Microsoft Graph.

  6. Verify that it appears in the actual OneDrive folder.

If you cannot register an app or ATTAIR blocks user consent, stop here and request the necessary approval from IT. There is no reliable way to bypass that organisational restriction.

I would not spend another development cycle on the scanner until this test passes.

4. File validation and antivirus

Every uploaded file must pass these checks.

Check

Required behaviour

Must indicate PDF

File signature

One qualification: antivirus scanning cannot prove that a file is harmless. It detects known threats and suspicious structures; it cannot guarantee detection of every malicious PDF.

I would preserve the original PDF rather than automatically rewriting or flattening it during security checks. Aircraft records should not be silently altered.

5. Comments and tasks

This needs to be built into the data model from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

I would support three ways of creating tasks.

A. Comments typed in the scanner

Example:

Check the aircraft hours against the previous techlog.

The app sends the comment with the PDF. The server creates a task linked to that document.

B. Comments written directly on the PDF

The scanner should have an annotation tool supporting:

  • Sticky-note comments

  • Text annotations

  • Highlighted text with a comment

  • Page-specific comments

The annotation content and page number are saved as task records. Supported annotations are also embedded into the PDF.

C. Comments added later

Users can reopen an existing document record and add comments. These create new tasks linked to the original PDF.

If someone edits a PDF in an external PDF editor, they must re-import the revised PDF for its supported annotations to be extracted. We should not promise automatic detection of changes made in arbitrary external applications.

Each task should have an owner, creation date, source PDF, page number, status, and optional resolution comment.

10. The instruction I would give the coding agent

This is the implementation brief I would use. It deliberately prohibits rebuilding the scanner or skipping the proof-of-connection stage.

Writing

ATTAIR Techlog Scanner — Cloud Upload and Task System

Objective

Implement a reliable, cloud-based PDF submission system for the existing Flutter aircraft techlog scanner.

The existing scanner is working. Preserve it.

Do not rebuild, redesign or replace its camera, cropping, page navigation, PDF generation or existing scanning workflow.

Approved technology stack

  • Flutter: existing application

  • Background transfers: background_downloader 9.6.5, subject to project compatibility testing

  • Authentication: Firebase Authentication, email/password and email verification

  • Database: Cloud Firestore

  • Backend: Python FastAPI on Google Cloud Run

  • Temporary file storage: private Cloudflare R2 bucket

  • Antivirus: ClamAV with updated signatures

  • PDF validation and annotation extraction: PyMuPDF and qpdf

  • Final storage: Isaac's existing ATTAIR OneDrive account

  • OneDrive API: Microsoft Graph using an application registered specifically for this project

Mandatory implementation rules

  1. Work from a backup or Git checkpoint.

  2. Inspect the existing project before changing anything.

  3. Document current scanner functionality and existing dependencies.

  4. Do not change unrelated scanner code.

  5. Do not place Microsoft credentials, R2 credentials or backend secrets in Flutter.

  6. Do not use a Microsoft-owned first-party application ID.

  7. Never mark a file uploaded merely because an HTTP request succeeded.

  8. Preserve the original PDF.

  9. Never delete a local PDF before verified final delivery.

  10. Implement and test each phase independently.

Phase 0 — OneDrive proof of connection

Before implementing the upload system, register an application with its own client ID.

Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Implement the server-side authorisation flow.

Authenticate Isaac's ATTAIR account, upload a test PDF into the designated OneDrive folder and verify the resulting file ID and size.

If application registration or consent is blocked by ATTAIR's tenant, stop. Report the exact error. Do not attempt alternative first-party client IDs or unapproved authentication workarounds.

Phase 1 — Accounts and approvals

Implement Firebase email/password authentication and email verification.

New accounts have pending status.

An administrator can approve, reject or revoke users.

Only server-controlled approval records determine upload eligibility.

The scanner remains usable while approval is pending.

Phase 2 — Upload gateway

Implement a FastAPI service on Cloud Run.

Every upload must:

  • Require a valid Firebase ID token.

  • Check current approval status.

  • Have a unique upload ID.

  • Enforce a 10 MB maximum.

  • Verify the PDF signature and MIME type.

  • Calculate SHA-256.

  • Reject duplicate submissions safely.

  • Store a temporary copy in private R2 storage.

Phase 3 — Security validation

Use ClamAV with current virus signatures.

Use PyMuPDF and qpdf to inspect the PDF.

Reject corrupt PDFs and dangerous embedded active content.

Quarantine suspicious files.

Do not upload quarantined files to OneDrive.

Record the scan result and validation details.

Phase 4 — OneDrive delivery

Use the server-side Microsoft Graph connection.

Write only to the configured ATTAIR TECHLOG UPLOADS folder.

Retain verified temporary files when OneDrive is unavailable.

Retry failed deliveries without creating duplicates.

Verify the resulting OneDrive file ID, size and destination before setting the status to delivered.

Keep temporary copies for seven days after confirmed delivery, then delete them.

Phase 5 — Comments and tasks

Implement:

  • Typed comments associated with a PDF.

  • In-app PDF sticky notes and text annotations.

  • Highlight comments.

  • Extraction of supported annotations from submitted PDFs.

  • Comments added later to existing document records.

  • Task creation, assignment and status updates.

Every task must reference its source PDF and page number where applicable.

Phase 6 — Mobile integration

Integrate the upload queue into the existing scanner.

Save the PDF locally before starting upload.

Use native background transfer support.

Persist upload state across application restarts.

Retry interrupted transfers and reconcile server status.

Do not delete local documents until verified OneDrive delivery and explicit local retention rules permit it.

Phase 7 — Acceptance testing

Test Android and iOS separately.

Test valid PDFs, corrupt PDFs, EICAR antivirus test files, duplicate uploads, interrupted connections, expired tokens, revoked users, OneDrive outages and comment extraction.

Regression-test all existing scanner functionality.

Do not declare completion until the acceptance tests pass.

Reporting requirements

After each phase, report:

  • Files created or changed.

  • Exact dependencies and versions.

  • Tests executed.

  • Test results.

  • Known limitations.

  • Whether the phase is safe to proceed.

Do not silently skip failed tests or claim success without evidence.

If ATTAIR blocks that connection: I would use a Windows OneDrive Sync Bridge as the fallback. It would receive approved uploads and place them in your locally synchronised OneDrive folder. The official OneDrive sync client then transfers them to the cloud.

Microsoft Support+1
This requires a dedicated, reliably online Windows machine.

4. The folder structure

I would create one dedicated root folder:

Plain text
ATTAIR TECHLOG SCANS/ │ ├── AIRCRAFT 001/ │ ├── 2026/ │ │ ├── 1501.pdf │ │ ├── 1502.pdf │ │ └── 1503.pdf │ ├── AIRCRAFT 002/ │ └── 2026/ │ └── UPLOAD RECORDS/

The backend should prevent duplicate uploads, record the uploader, and verify the uploaded file before marking it complete.

5. Reliability rules I would make mandatory

  1. The phone saves every scan locally before submission.

  2. Uploads can resume after the app closes or internet disconnects.

  3. Every upload has a unique ID to prevent duplicates.

  4. The server checks user approval on every upload, not just at login.

  5. Revoking a user blocks future uploads.

  6. The server verifies the OneDrive upload before acknowledging success.

  7. Failed uploads remain queued and are retried.

  8. The app never deletes the local PDF merely because the upload request was sent.

Flutter + Firebase + Microsoft Graph delegated connection owned by you.

My final recommendation: a small upload gateway + OneDrive

I would not use Telegram, email or Dropbox as the primary architecture.

I would build a small private upload website/API, with a lightweight backend, and connect that backend to your ATTAIR OneDrive through a Windows OneDrive Sync Bridge.

This avoids Microsoft OAuth inside the mobile app entirely. It also avoids giving every user access to your storage account.

The workflow is:

  1. User scans a techlog.

  2. App creates a PDF.

  3. App submits the PDF automatically to your upload server.

  4. Server verifies the file and checks it for malicious content.

  5. Server places the verified PDF in a local folder synchronised by your ATTAIR OneDrive desktop client.

  6. OneDrive synchronises it to your cloud account.

  7. Your app receives confirmation after the file is verified in the OneDrive destination.

2. Exact upload workflow

1. Scanner creates PDF

PDF is saved permanently in the app's local documents directory before any network operation.

2. Upload gateway receives PDF

Checks the user's approval, file size, file signature and upload ID.

3. Quarantine and validation

Stores a temporary copy in R2, scans it with ClamAV, parses the PDF and checks for dangerous embedded content.

4. OneDrive delivery

Cloud Run uses your authorised Microsoft connection to upload the clean PDF.

5. Delivery verification

Checks the returned OneDrive file ID, file size and destination before marking the upload complete.

Delivered to ATTAIR OneDrive

Temporary copy is retained for seven days, then deleted automatically.

If OneDrive is unavailable, the verified PDF remains in R2 with status Awaiting OneDrive delivery. The server retries. It does not ask the user to scan again.

3. OneDrive connection: the first and most important test

Your account is:

isaac.eke@attair.com.ng

I would use a single server-side Microsoft Graph delegated connection, authorised by you once.

The application registration must belong to your own project. We will not reuse the Microsoft-owned client ID that caused AADSTS65002.

The intended permissions are:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Files.ReadWrite allows the application to write files to the signed-in user's OneDrive without inherently requiring administrator consent. However, ATTAIR's tenant policy can still require administrator approval.

Microsoft Learn+1

Important security limitation: This delegated permission is broader than one folder. The backend will be programmed to write only to ATTAIR Techlog Uploads, but the underlying Microsoft token has access to your OneDrive files more broadly. Its credentials must never be exposed to the mobile app.

The go/no-go test

Before implementing the rest of the system:

  1. Register your own application in Microsoft Entra.

  2. Configure its server-side redirect URI.

  3. Sign in using your ATTAIR account.

  4. Authorise the delegated permissions.

  5. Upload one test PDF through Microsoft Graph.

  6. Verify that it appears in the actual OneDrive folder.

If you cannot register an app or ATTAIR blocks user consent, stop here and request the necessary approval from IT. There is no reliable way to bypass that organisational restriction.

I would not spend another development cycle on the scanner until this test passes.

4. File validation and antivirus

Every uploaded file must pass these checks.

Check

Required behaviour

Extension

Must be .pdf

MIME type

Must indicate PDF

File signature

Must successfully parse the document

Structural check

A file that fails validation goes into quarantine. It never reaches OneDrive.

One qualification: antivirus scanning cannot prove that a file is harmless. It detects known threats and suspicious structures; it cannot guarantee detection of every malicious PDF.

I would preserve the original PDF rather than automatically rewriting or flattening it during security checks. Aircraft records should not be silently altered.

5. Comments and tasks

This needs to be built into the data model from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

I would support three ways of creating tasks.

A. Comments typed in the scanner

Example:

Check the aircraft hours against the previous techlog.

The app sends the comment with the PDF. The server creates a task linked to that document.

B. Comments written directly on the PDF

The scanner should have an annotation tool supporting:

  • Sticky-note comments

  • Text annotations

  • Highlighted text with a comment

  • Page-specific comments

The annotation content and page number are saved as task records. Supported annotations are also embedded into the PDF.

C. Comments added later

Users can reopen an existing document record and add comments. These create new tasks linked to the original PDF.

If someone edits a PDF in an external PDF editor, they must re-import the revised PDF for its supported annotations to be extracted. We should not promise automatic detection of changes made in arbitrary external applications.

Each task should have an owner, creation date, source PDF, page number, status, and optional resolution comment.

10. The instruction I would give the coding agent

This is the implementation brief I would use. It deliberately prohibits rebuilding the scanner or skipping the proof-of-connection stage.

Writing

ATTAIR Techlog Scanner — Cloud Upload and Task System

Objective

Implement a reliable, cloud-based PDF submission system for the existing Flutter aircraft techlog scanner.

The existing scanner is working. Preserve it.

Do not rebuild, redesign or replace its camera, cropping, page navigation, PDF generation or existing scanning workflow.

Approved technology stack

  • Flutter: existing application

  • Background transfers: background_downloader 9.6.5, subject to project compatibility testing

  • Authentication: Firebase Authentication, email/password and email verification

  • Database: Cloud Firestore

  • Backend: Python FastAPI on Google Cloud Run

  • Temporary file storage: private Cloudflare R2 bucket

  • Antivirus: ClamAV with updated signatures

  • PDF validation and annotation extraction: PyMuPDF and qpdf

  • Final storage: Isaac's existing ATTAIR OneDrive account

  • OneDrive API: Microsoft Graph using an application registered specifically for this project

Mandatory implementation rules

  1. Work from a backup or Git checkpoint.

  2. Inspect the existing project before changing anything.

  3. Document current scanner functionality and existing dependencies.

  4. Do not change unrelated scanner code.

  5. Do not place Microsoft credentials, R2 credentials or backend secrets in Flutter.

  6. Do not use a Microsoft-owned first-party application ID.

  7. Never mark a file uploaded merely because an HTTP request succeeded.

  8. Preserve the original PDF.

  9. Never delete a local PDF before verified final delivery.

  10. Implement and test each phase independently.

Phase 0 — OneDrive proof of connection

Before implementing the upload system, register an application with its own client ID.

Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Implement the server-side authorisation flow.

Authenticate Isaac's ATTAIR account, upload a test PDF into the designated OneDrive folder and verify the resulting file ID and size.

If application registration or consent is blocked by ATTAIR's tenant, stop. Report the exact error. Do not attempt alternative first-party client IDs or unapproved authentication workarounds.

Phase 1 — Accounts and approvals

Implement Firebase email/password authentication and email verification.

New accounts have pending status.

An administrator can approve, reject or revoke users.

Only server-controlled approval records determine upload eligibility.

The scanner remains usable while approval is pending.

Phase 2 — Upload gateway

Implement a FastAPI service on Cloud Run.

Every upload must:

  • Require a valid Firebase ID token.

  • Check current approval status.

  • Have a unique upload ID.

  • Enforce a 10 MB maximum.

  • Verify the PDF signature and MIME type.

  • Calculate SHA-256.

  • Reject duplicate submissions safely.

  • Store a temporary copy in private R2 storage.

Phase 3 — Security validation

Use ClamAV with current virus signatures.

Use PyMuPDF and qpdf to inspect the PDF.

Reject corrupt PDFs and dangerous embedded active content.

Quarantine suspicious files.

Do not upload quarantined files to OneDrive.

Record the scan result and validation details.

Phase 4 — OneDrive delivery

Use the server-side Microsoft Graph connection.

Write only to the configured ATTAIR TECHLOG UPLOADS folder.

Retain verified temporary files when OneDrive is unavailable.

Retry failed deliveries without creating duplicates.

Verify the resulting OneDrive file ID, size and destination before setting the status to delivered.

Keep temporary copies for seven days after confirmed delivery, then delete them.

Phase 5 — Comments and tasks

Implement:

  • Typed comments associated with a PDF.

  • In-app PDF sticky notes and text annotations.

  • Highlight comments.

  • Extraction of supported annotations from submitted PDFs.

  • Comments added later to existing document records.

  • Task creation, assignment and status updates.

Every task must reference its source PDF and page number where applicable.

Phase 6 — Mobile integration

Integrate the upload queue into the existing scanner.

Save the PDF locally before starting upload.

Use native background transfer support.

Persist upload state across application restarts.

Retry interrupted transfers and reconcile server status.

Do not delete local documents until verified OneDrive delivery and explicit local retention rules permit it.

Phase 7 — Acceptance testing

Test Android and iOS separately.

Test valid PDFs, corrupt PDFs, EICAR antivirus test files, duplicate uploads, interrupted connections, expired tokens, revoked users, OneDrive outages and comment extraction.

Regression-test all existing scanner functionality.

Do not declare completion until the acceptance tests pass.

Reporting requirements

After each phase, report:

  • Files created or changed.

  • Exact dependencies and versions.

  • Tests executed.

  • Test results.

  • Known limitations.

  • Whether the phase is safe to proceed.

Do not silently skip failed tests or claim success without evidence.

3. How your OneDrive receives the PDFs

This is the critical part.

I would build a server-side OneDrive connection using Microsoft Graph and your ATTAIR account.

Approved user's phone

PDF submitted over HTTPS

Secure upload server

Checks approval, validates PDF and queues upload

Microsoft Graph

Uses your separately authorised ATTAIR connection

Your OneDrive

isaac.eke@attair.com.ng

Your OneDrive connection is established once, by you. The backend stores its credentials securely. Users never receive those credentials.

Microsoft's delegated Files.ReadWrite permission can upload files to the signed-in user's OneDrive and is listed as not inherently requiring administrator consent. However, ATTAIR tenant policies can still prevent you from granting consent. This permission also grants broad access to your files, so the backend must strictly limit its operations to the designated folder.

Microsoft Learn+2

If ATTAIR blocks that connection: I would use a Windows OneDrive Sync Bridge as the fallback. It would receive approved uploads and place them in your locally synchronised OneDrive folder. The official OneDrive sync client then transfers them to the cloud.

Microsoft Support+1
This requires a dedicated, reliably online Windows machine.

4. The folder structure

I would create one dedicated root folder:

Plain text
ATTAIR TECHLOG SCANS/ │ ├── AIRCRAFT 001/ │ ├── 2026/ │ │ ├── 1501.pdf │ │ ├── 1502.pdf │ │ └── 1503.pdf │ ├── AIRCRAFT 002/ │ └── 2026/ │ └── UPLOAD RECORDS/

The backend should prevent duplicate uploads, record the uploader, and verify the uploaded file before marking it complete.

5. Reliability rules I would make mandatory

  1. The phone saves every scan locally before submission.

  2. Uploads can resume after the app closes or internet disconnects.

  3. Every upload has a unique ID to prevent duplicates.

  4. The server checks user approval on every upload, not just at login.

  5. Revoking a user blocks future uploads.

  6. The server verifies the OneDrive upload before acknowledging success.

  7. Failed uploads remain queued and are retried.

  8. The app never deletes the local PDF merely because the upload request was sent.

My final architectural decision

Recommended
Flutter + Firebase + Microsoft Graph delegated connection owned by you.

This removes Microsoft sign-in from the users' experience, centralises approvals, and keeps your OneDrive private.

There is one dependency we must test before committing to the Graph implementation: whether your ATTAIR tenant permits you to register an application and consent to delegated Files.ReadWrite. If not, use the OneDrive Sync Bridge rather than repeatedly attempting different OAuth packages.

The first milestone should be very small: register one test account, approve it, upload one PDF, and verify that the PDF appears in your actual ATTAIR OneDrive folder. Only after that succeeds should the working scanner be connected to it.

My final recommendation: a small upload gateway + OneDrive

I would not use Telegram, email or Dropbox as the primary architecture.

I would build a small private upload website/API, with a lightweight backend, and connect that backend to your ATTAIR OneDrive through a Windows OneDrive Sync Bridge.

This avoids Microsoft OAuth inside the mobile app entirely. It also avoids giving every user access to your storage account.

The workflow is:

  1. User scans a techlog.

  2. App creates a PDF.

  3. App submits the PDF automatically to your upload server.

  4. Server verifies the file and checks it for malicious content.

  5. Server places the verified PDF in a local folder synchronised by your ATTAIR OneDrive desktop client.

  6. OneDrive synchronises it to your cloud account.

  7. Your app receives confirmation after the file is verified in the OneDrive destination.

Telegram's official Bot API currently supports uploads up to 50 MB and downloads up to 20 MB through its hosted API. That download restriction makes it unsuitable as the central PDF transport mechanism if files might exceed 20 MB.

Telegram+1

Dropbox Help+1

Supabase's free storage upload limit is 50 MB per file. It does not provide unlimited uploads.

Supabase Docs

There is no credible service I would promise offers unlimited free uploads forever. We should avoid building the application around that assumption.

5. The reliability requirements

These are non-negotiable:

  1. Local PDF saved before upload.

  2. Upload queue survives app closure and phone restart.

  3. Automatic retry after internet interruption.

  4. Server acknowledges receipt only after validation.

  5. OneDrive status remains separate from server-received status.

  6. Unique upload IDs prevent duplicates.

  7. No local PDF deletion until OneDrive synchronisation is confirmed.

  8. Failed uploads are visible and can be retried manually.

The app should show three distinct statuses:

  • Saved on phone

  • Received and verified

  • Stored in ATTAIR OneDrive

That prevents the app from claiming success prematurely.

This is a deliberate separation: authentication, upload, virus scanning, task management and final storage do not depend on the same service.

Why these choices?

  • background_downloader uses native Android WorkManager and Apple's background URLSession mechanisms. It supports persistent transfer tracking and retry behaviour.

    Dart API docs+2

  • Firebase provides user authentication and a database for approval and task records.

    Firebase+1

  • Cloudflare R2 gives us a temporary storage area with a 10 GB monthly free storage allowance and free internet egress.

    Cloudflare R2 docs+1

2. Exact upload workflow

1. Scanner creates PDF

PDF is saved permanently in the app's local documents directory before any network operation.

2. Upload gateway receives PDF

Checks the user's approval, file size, file signature and upload ID.

3. Quarantine and validation

Stores a temporary copy in R2, scans it with ClamAV, parses the PDF and checks for dangerous embedded content.

4. OneDrive delivery

Cloud Run uses your authorised Microsoft connection to upload the clean PDF.

5. Delivery verification

Checks the returned OneDrive file ID, file size and destination before marking the upload complete.

Delivered to ATTAIR OneDrive

Temporary copy is retained for seven days, then deleted automatically.

If OneDrive is unavailable, the verified PDF remains in R2 with status Awaiting OneDrive delivery. The server retries. It does not ask the user to scan again.

3. OneDrive connection: the first and most important test

Your account is:

isaac.eke@attair.com.ng

I would use a single server-side Microsoft Graph delegated connection, authorised by you once.

The application registration must belong to your own project. We will not reuse the Microsoft-owned client ID that caused AADSTS65002.

The intended permissions are:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Files.ReadWrite allows the application to write files to the signed-in user's OneDrive without inherently requiring administrator consent. However, ATTAIR's tenant policy can still require administrator approval.

Microsoft Learn+1

Important security limitation: This delegated permission is broader than one folder. The backend will be programmed to write only to ATTAIR Techlog Uploads, but the underlying Microsoft token has access to your OneDrive files more broadly. Its credentials must never be exposed to the mobile app.

The go/no-go test

Before implementing the rest of the system:

  1. Register your own application in Microsoft Entra.

  2. Configure its server-side redirect URI.

  3. Sign in using your ATTAIR account.

  4. Authorise the delegated permissions.

  5. Upload one test PDF through Microsoft Graph.

  6. Verify that it appears in the actual OneDrive folder.

If you cannot register an app or ATTAIR blocks user consent, stop here and request the necessary approval from IT. There is no reliable way to bypass that organisational restriction.

I would not spend another development cycle on the scanner until this test passes.

4. File validation and antivirus

Every uploaded file must pass these checks.

Check

Required behaviour

Extension

Must be .pdf

MIME type

Must indicate PDF

File signature

Must contain a valid PDF header

PDF parser

Must successfully parse the document

Structural check

qpdf must report no structural errors

Malware scan

ClamAV must report clean

Active content

Reject dangerous JavaScript, launch actions and embedded executable content

File size

Maximum 10 MB

Duplicate detection

SHA-256 hash and unique upload ID

A file that fails validation goes into quarantine. It never reaches OneDrive.

One qualification: antivirus scanning cannot prove that a file is harmless. It detects known threats and suspicious structures; it cannot guarantee detection of every malicious PDF.

I would preserve the original PDF rather than automatically rewriting or flattening it during security checks. Aircraft records should not be silently altered.

5. Comments and tasks

This needs to be built into the data model from the beginning, not added as an afterthought.

I would support three ways of creating tasks.

A. Comments typed in the scanner

Example:

Check the aircraft hours against the previous techlog.

The app sends the comment with the PDF. The server creates a task linked to that document.

B. Comments written directly on the PDF

The scanner should have an annotation tool supporting:

  • Sticky-note comments

  • Text annotations

  • Highlighted text with a comment

  • Page-specific comments

The annotation content and page number are saved as task records. Supported annotations are also embedded into the PDF.

C. Comments added later

Users can reopen an existing document record and add comments. These create new tasks linked to the original PDF.

If someone edits a PDF in an external PDF editor, they must re-import the revised PDF for its supported annotations to be extracted. We should not promise automatic detection of changes made in arbitrary external applications.

Example task screen

Techlog tasks

AIRCRAFT 001 · TECHLOG 1501

Open

Check aircraft hours against previous techlog

Page 2 · Comment from Pilot A

TECHLOG 1502

In progress

Verify landing time entry

Page 1 · PDF annotation

TECHLOG 1503

Completed

Confirm missing signature

Page 3 · Comment from Pilot B

Each task should have an owner, creation date, source PDF, page number, status, and optional resolution comment.

I would configure usage alerts, limit Cloud Run instances and keep R2 staging files on a short retention period. An alert is not a hard spending cap, so billing must also be monitored.

7. Mobile reliability

For Flutter, I would use background_downloader version 9.6.5 as the initial candidate, subject to compatibility testing with your existing Flutter project.

It uses:

  • Android WorkManager for persistent background work.

  • iOS background URLSession for background file transfers.

  • Persistent task tracking and retry support.

    Dart API docs+1

The app must also maintain its own upload queue in local storage.

One limitation must be explicit: neither Android nor iOS guarantees that a background transfer will continue after a user force-stops or force-quits the app. The app must reconcile and retry when reopened.

10. The instruction I would give the coding agent

This is the implementation brief I would use. It deliberately prohibits rebuilding the scanner or skipping the proof-of-connection stage.

Writing

ATTAIR Techlog Scanner — Cloud Upload and Task System

Objective

Implement a reliable, cloud-based PDF submission system for the existing Flutter aircraft techlog scanner.

The existing scanner is working. Preserve it.

Do not rebuild, redesign or replace its camera, cropping, page navigation, PDF generation or existing scanning workflow.

Approved technology stack

  • Flutter: existing application

  • Background transfers: background_downloader 9.6.5, subject to project compatibility testing

  • Authentication: Firebase Authentication, email/password and email verification

  • Database: Cloud Firestore

  • Backend: Python FastAPI on Google Cloud Run

  • Temporary file storage: private Cloudflare R2 bucket

  • Antivirus: ClamAV with updated signatures

  • PDF validation and annotation extraction: PyMuPDF and qpdf

  • Final storage: Isaac's existing ATTAIR OneDrive account

  • OneDrive API: Microsoft Graph using an application registered specifically for this project

Mandatory implementation rules

  1. Work from a backup or Git checkpoint.

  2. Inspect the existing project before changing anything.

  3. Document current scanner functionality and existing dependencies.

  4. Do not change unrelated scanner code.

  5. Do not place Microsoft credentials, R2 credentials or backend secrets in Flutter.

  6. Do not use a Microsoft-owned first-party application ID.

  7. Never mark a file uploaded merely because an HTTP request succeeded.

  8. Preserve the original PDF.

  9. Never delete a local PDF before verified final delivery.

  10. Implement and test each phase independently.

Phase 0 — OneDrive proof of connection

Before implementing the upload system, register an application with its own client ID.

Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions:

  • User.Read

  • Files.ReadWrite

  • offline_access

Implement the server-side authorisation flow.

Authenticate Isaac's ATTAIR account, upload a test PDF into the designated OneDrive folder and verify the resulting file ID and size.

If application registration or consent is blocked by ATTAIR's tenant, stop. Report the exact error. Do not attempt alternative first-party client IDs or unapproved authentication workarounds.

Phase 1 — Accounts and approvals

Implement Firebase email/password authentication and email verification.

New accounts have pending status.

An administrator can approve, reject or revoke users.

Only server-controlled approval records determine upload eligibility.

The scanner remains usable while approval is pending.

Phase 2 — Upload gateway

Implement a FastAPI service on Cloud Run.

Every upload must:

  • Require a valid Firebase ID token.

  • Check current approval status.

  • Have a unique upload ID.

  • Enforce a 10 MB maximum.

  • Verify the PDF signature and MIME type.

  • Calculate SHA-256.

  • Reject duplicate submissions safely.

  • Store a temporary copy in private R2 storage.

Phase 3 — Security validation

Use ClamAV with current virus signatures.

Use PyMuPDF and qpdf to inspect the PDF.

Reject corrupt PDFs and dangerous embedded active content.

Quarantine suspicious files.

Do not upload quarantined files to OneDrive.

Record the scan result and validation details.

Phase 4 — OneDrive delivery

Use the server-side Microsoft Graph connection.

Write only to the configured ATTAIR TECHLOG UPLOADS folder.

Retain verified temporary files when OneDrive is unavailable.

Retry failed deliveries without creating duplicates.

Verify the resulting OneDrive file ID, size and destination before setting the status to delivered.

Keep temporary copies for seven days after confirmed delivery, then delete them.

Phase 5 — Comments and tasks

Implement:

  • Typed comments associated with a PDF.

  • In-app PDF sticky notes and text annotations.

  • Highlight comments.

  • Extraction of supported annotations from submitted PDFs.

  • Comments added later to existing document records.

  • Task creation, assignment and status updates.

Every task must reference its source PDF and page number where applicable.

Phase 6 — Mobile integration

Integrate the upload queue into the existing scanner.

Save the PDF locally before starting upload.

Use native background transfer support.

Persist upload state across application restarts.

Retry interrupted transfers and reconcile server status.

Do not delete local documents until verified OneDrive delivery and explicit local retention rules permit it.

Phase 7 — Acceptance testing

Test Android and iOS separately.

Test valid PDFs, corrupt PDFs, EICAR antivirus test files, duplicate uploads, interrupted connections, expired tokens, revoked users, OneDrive outages and comment extraction.

Regression-test all existing scanner functionality.

Do not declare completion until the acceptance tests pass.

Reporting requirements

After each phase, report:

  • Files created or changed.

  • Exact dependencies and versions.

  • Tests executed.

  • Test results.

  • Known limitations.

  • Whether the phase is safe to proceed.

Do not silently skip failed tests or claim success without evidence.

11. The only thing I would do first

Critical dependency

Test the ATTAIR OneDrive connection before writing the rest of the system.

That is the one part we cannot control from your application: whether ATTAIR allows your account to register and authorise the delegated Graph application.

Everything else can be built independently and tested without touching the working scanner.

If that connection succeeds, the rest of the architecture is implementable without a Windows bridge, without individual users needing OneDrive accounts, and without Microsoft OAuth inside the mobile app.

If it fails because ATTAIR requires administrator consent, we stop and resolve that specific permission issue rather than rebuilding the authentication system again.
